title: Comparative Tangkhul: Lexical and Phonological Reconstruction
alternate_titles: Reconstruction of Proto-Tangkhul Phonology and Dialect Geography
journal: UC Berkeley Sino-Tibetan Linguistic Monograph Series
publisher: Department of Linguistics, University of California, Berkeley
subject: Comparative Tibeto-Burman Linguistics & Dialectology
notes: Pioneering comparative study reconstructing Proto-Tangkhul onsets, vowels, and tonal categories across 5 sister varieties.
abstract: This paper presents a preliminary lexical and phonological reconstruction of Proto-Tangkhul (PTk), the ancestral mother language of the Tangkhulic branch within the Tibeto-Burman family. Based on extensive field data collected across Ukhrul (Standard Tangkhul), Huishu, Kachai, East Tusom, and Phadang, we establish regular sound correspondences between onset stops, liquid clusters (*pl-, *kl-, *pr-, *kr-), and vowel developments. We demonstrate that Standard Tangkhul underwent lenition of syllable codas while peripheral varieties like Huishu and Tusom preserved archaic conservative distinctions.

sections.title: 1. Introduction & Genetic Subgrouping
sections.content: The Tangkhulic languages, spoken primarily in Ukhrul and Kamjong districts of Manipur and adjoining regions of Myanmar, constitute an independent, deeply conservative branch of Tibeto-Burman. Grierson (1903) categorized them under the generic rubric 'Kuki-Chin-Naga', but subsequent historical work (Matisoff 1972, Burling 2003) confirmed their discrete genetic status. Standard Tangkhul (Ukhrul) functions as the literary standard and regional lingua franca, yet individual villages preserve distinct daughter languages with varying degrees of mutual intelligibility.

sections.title: 2. Phonological Correspondences & Syllable Structure
sections.content: Proto-Tangkhul possessed a sesquisyllabic or disyllabic structure *Cə-CVC. Modern Standard Tangkhul preserves the unstressed nominalizing/adjectival prefix *kə- (written ka-) and negative *mə- (written ma-). In Kachai, these prefixes undergo secondary voicing assimilation (gə- / bə-). In coda position, Proto-Tangkhul *-(k, t, p) are realized as unreleased glottal stops or weak stops in Ukhrul, whereas final *-l is lost in Ukhrul but preserved in Huishu.

Loss of final liquid *-l in standard Ukhrul.

sections.title: 3. Tonal Categories & Pitch Contours
sections.content: Proto-Tangkhul tones correlate systematically with syllable coda sonorancy and proto-voicing. Standard Ukhrul distinguishes three level tones: High (55), Mid (33), and Low (22). Stems ending in original voiceless stops condition High abrupt pitch, whereas sonorant codas allow tonal register contrasts that interact with morphological suffixation.
